content: Vitamin D deficiency is categorized into two primary groups: deficient and insufficient, based on serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) levels, as per the Global Consensus Recommendations on the Prevention and Management of Nutritional Rickets and the Institute of Medicine (IOM). The deficiency can be further subdivided into mild, moderate, and severe categories depending on the degree of deficiency. Another classification system considers the etiology of vitamin D deficiency, dividing it into acquired or inherited forms. According to the Global Consensus Recommendations and the IOM, vitamin D deficiency is classified into two groups—deficient and insufficient—based on serum 25(OH)D3 levels. The Australian Family Physician categorizes vitamin D deficiency into three groups based on serum 25(OH)D levels. Vitamin D deficiency can also be classified into two major groups, acquired or inherited, depending on its underlying cause.
